ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $CD$ is the altitude on the hypotenuse $AB$, and $\angle ACD=40^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since in the right-angled triangle $ABC$, $CD$ is the altitude on the hypotenuse $AB$\\
Therefore, $\angle ACB=\angle CDB=90^\circ$\\
Since $\angle ACD=40^\circ$\\
Therefore, $\angle BCD=90^\circ-40^\circ=50^\circ$\\
In $\triangle BCD$, $\angle B=180^\circ-90^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: A, D, and B lie on the same horizontal line, C is above them, CD is drawn from C to D on AB, and the marked angle at C between CA and CD is the given 40°. From the text, use that AB is the hypotenuse of right triangle ABC, so ∠ACB is 90°, and CD is an altitude to AB, so ∠ADC is 90°. Since D lies on AB, ∠CAD is the same angle as ∠CAB. Therefore triangles ACD and ABC are similar by AA similarity: ∠ADC corresponds to ∠ACB, and the shared A-angle corresponds to itself. Under this correspondence, ∠ACD corresponds to ∠ABC, so ∠B = ∠ACD = 40°.
